title: A merge_failed refusal names no conflicting file
description:
epic-wne stopped twice on this refusal, verbatim:

  merge_failed: attempt 2 of mrn does not merge onto epic/wne:

The sentence ends in a colon and a space. The reason field is EMPTY.

A merge conflict is the one refusal where 'which files' IS the answer. Every other stop
carries its evidence - a gate refusal names the check and keys the record to the commit
it ran on, a stall warning names the branch and the worktree and how long each has been
still. This one names nothing, so the operator has to reconstruct the merge by hand to
learn anything at all. I did, and it took a worktree, a fetch of the attempt branch and
a --no-commit merge to find out the answer was two files:

  CONFLICT (add/add): internal/runconfig/worktype.go
  CONFLICT (add/add): internal/runconfig/worktype_test.go

That is information git printed and the reconciler discarded.

WHAT TO FIX: carry git's conflict output into the refusal detail. At minimum the
conflicting paths and the conflict kind (add/add, content, delete/modify), because the
kind is what tells an operator whether this is two workers colliding or a rebase gone
stale. The full merge output is better still - the refusal is already a paragraph, and
nobody reading it is short of screen.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CONVENIENCE: an add/add conflict is the signature of a PLANNING
defect - two same-wave ticks creating one file, which is what happened here. A refusal
that named the kind would have said 'your wave is wrong' in the feed instead of leaving
it to be diagnosed. The orchestrator can see this and is throwing it away.
acceptance_criteria: A merge_failed refusal carries the conflicting paths and the conflict kind from git's own output, an add/add conflict is distinguishable from a content conflict in the run feed without reproducing the merge, and a test asserts the detail is non-empty for a real conflict
